sections.html:
Seventeen miles west of Portland, and just west of Beaverton, Hillsboro is where Washington County keeps its courthouse. The city sits in the Tualatin Valley, the stretch of the metro area people call the Silicon Forest. Voters elect a mayor and six at-large councilors, and a city manager handles day-to-day work. Inside the city limits there are about 21.6 square miles of land.

The city counted 91,611 people in 2010 and 106,447 in 2020, with 111,126 estimated for July 1, 2025. Growth like that produced older bungalows near downtown and much newer homes toward the edges. Of 42,363 housing units, about half are renter-occupied, so plenty of owners selling are landlords with tenants already living in the house.

Two offices matter most when you sell: city planning and building staff, who handle permits, and the county's Assessment and Taxation office, which handles tax bills and recording.

sections.h2: Where you live in Hillsboro matters
sections.html:
Hillsboro is a collection of districts, and the right approach for a downtown house differs from one in a newer subdivision.

  • Downtown: the original core around the county courthouse, with the oldest homes.
  • Orenco and Orenco Station: a transit-oriented neighborhood built around the light rail line.
  • Tanasbourne and Amberglen: the retail and office area on the eastern edge, near Beaverton.
  • Hawthorn Farm and the Fair Complex: home to Westside Commons, with the Intel campus nearby.
  • South Hillsboro: the newest planned district, annexed in recent years.
  • Witch Hazel Village, Quatama and NE 28th Avenue: plan areas with a mix of older and newer housing.

South Hillsboro is master planned across about 1,400 acres, with an estimated 8,000 homes, more than 285 acres of parks and open space and about 15 miles of new trails. Sellers of older houses nearby compete with that new construction, and buyers often compare the two.

Intel employs about 20,000 people across its Ronler Acres, Jones Farm and Hawthorn Farm campuses, making it the biggest private employer. Nike, Tokyo Electron America, Amazon, the school district and the county also employ thousands. Manufacturing makes up about 24 percent of local jobs, and health care, education and social services about 15 percent. When work shifts at one of the big employers, an owner may need to sell on a short timeline.

sections.h2: Roads, light rail and the airport
sections.html:
Oregon Route 8 (Tualatin Valley Highway) carries east-west commuters, and U.S. Route 26 crosses the northeast corner. Oregon Route 219, Cornelius Pass Road and Brookwood Parkway handle north-south traffic. The MAX Blue Line has served Hillsboro since 1998 and ends at Hatfield Government Center, and in 2024 the MAX Red Line was extended from the Beaverton Transit Center to the Fairgrounds station.

Homes within walking distance of a station are easier to market to commuters. Homes under a busy flight path or beside a major road may need a different pitch. Hillsboro Airport is the second-busiest in Oregon after Portland International, and the Oregon International Air Show is held there each summer.

Summers are mild and the wet season is long. August is warmest, with an average high near 81 degrees, and January highs average about 46. Annual precipitation is about 36 inches over roughly 160 days, mostly November through March, and relative humidity averages 77 percent. The record high is 114 degrees, set on June 28, 2021.

  • Moss and worn shingles on the roof
  • Gutters, downspouts and drainage near the foundation
  • Damp crawl spaces and exterior wood rot
  • Older windows that leak air or water

A house with these problems usually needs more than fresh paint to pass a buyer's inspection, which is where as-is sales appeal to some owners.

A sale here carries Washington County's real estate transfer tax, which is one dollar per thousand dollars of the price. The county treats responsibility as something the buyer and seller sort out between them. Pay it, or file for an exemption, within 15 days of the deed being recorded. A late penalty follows after that.

The county waives or exempts the tax for these transfers when the right paperwork is filed:

  • Property passed by gift, will or inheritance
  • A deed given in lieu of foreclosure, or a transfer a court orders
  • A trustee's deed after foreclosure
  • Transfers under $13,999
  • A transfer between spouses ordered by a court in a divorce or separation

The county explains how to apply on its transfer tax exemption page.

The county mails statements on or before October 25.

A weekend or holiday pushes the date to the next business day.

To contest a value, go to the Board of Property Tax Appeals before December 31. The taxed value begins with whichever is lower, real market value or maximum assessed value, and the maximum can climb by no more than 3 percent in a year. Prepaid property taxes are generally not accepted, so ask your title company how this year's bill will be split between you and the buyer. Official answers sit in the Washington County property tax FAQ.

Oregon home sales normally include a signed property disclosure statement. ORS 105.464 sends it to every buyer who writes an offer, and that buyer may revoke in writing within five days of delivery unless the right was waived.

Certain sales fall outside the rule: court-appointed personal representatives and trustees, lenders that took a home by foreclosure or deed in lieu, and the first sale of a never-occupied home. A seller who is covered but withholds the form lets the buyer walk away any time before closing. Since the answers reflect your own knowledge, record leaks, repairs and permits you remember.

• Rental houses: landlords with tenants in place.
  • Inherited houses: estate sales often skip the standard disclosure form and may qualify for a transfer tax exemption.
  • Deferred maintenance: wet-season damage adds up when repairs wait.
  • Timing: a job move tied to a tech employer can leave little time for a long listing.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works in Hillsboro
sections.html:
Because a cash buyer is not borrowing, no lender approval slows things down. Request an offer, let the buyer view the house, and if you accept, the title company prepares the documents and files the deed at the county.

Transfer tax, the tax split and any liens do not disappear, and each shows on the settlement sheet. Have the figures in writing before signing. If you lean toward listing, set a cash number next to repair bills, commissions and months of upkeep. Your timeline and the condition of the house usually decide it.

faqs.q: How many people live in Hillsboro, Oregon?
faqs.a: The estimate for July 1, 2025 is 111,126 residents, up from 106,447 in the 2020 census and 91,611 in 2010.
Hillsboro is in Washington County and is its county seat. Property tax bills, recording and transfer tax all go through Washington County offices.

faqs.q: Is there a transfer tax when I sell a house in Hillsboro?
faqs.a: Yes. Washington County charges one dollar per thousand dollars of the selling price, and liability is between buyer and seller. The county lists exemptions, such as inheritance transfers and deeds in lieu of foreclosure.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Washington County?
faqs.a: Payments are due November 15, February 15 and May 15, with the next business day counting if a date lands on a weekend or holiday. Paying in full by November 15 earns a 3 percent discount.

faqs.q: Do I have to give the buyer a disclosure form in Oregon?
faqs.a: In most sales, yes. ORS 105.464 requires the seller to deliver the statement to each buyer who makes a written offer, and the buyer can revoke within five days unless that right was waived. Sales by estates, trustees and foreclosing lenders are among the exclusions.
